# backend-capability Specification

<!-- Generated by Prism from prism/spec.json. Change the app through your agent with /prism, not by editing this file. -->

## Purpose

Backend capability: Decide, as a DMN decision table with hit policy FIRST, which backend capability serves a front end feature at a site that is online or air-gapped: the verified guest, the static model record, acceptance-vector replay, the fingerprint check, the proof bundled with the site, or a link to the CI attestation.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Never attestation-link when site is airgapped

The app SHALL NOT answer `attestation-link` when site is airgapped, because nothing at an air-gapped site ever reaches for the network.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-001, theorem `inv001Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-001 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `verdict-card airgapped` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `attestation-link`
- **AND** the app answers `guest-dispatch`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: Always fingerprint-check when feature is seal-badge

The app SHALL answer `fingerprint-check` when feature is seal-badge, because the seal is always recomputed, never trusted as text.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-002, theorem `inv002Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-002 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `seal-badge online` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `fingerprint-check`
- **AND** the app answers `fingerprint-check`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: Always guest-dispatch when feature is verdict-card

The app SHALL answer `guest-dispatch` when feature is verdict-card, because every answer comes from the verified guest.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-003, theorem `inv003Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-003 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `verdict-card airgapped` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `guest-dispatch`
- **AND** the app answers `guest-dispatch`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: REQ-001 fingerprint-check when feature is seal-badge

The app SHALL answer `fingerprint-check` when feature is seal-badge, because the seal is the fingerprint, recomputed in the browser.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule1`).

#### Scenario: REQ-001 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `seal-badge online` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `fingerprint-check`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: REQ-002 guest-dispatch when feature is verdict-card

The app SHALL answer `guest-dispatch` when feature is verdict-card and no earlier rule matches, because the answer is computed by the verified guest, never by a server.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule2`).

#### Scenario: REQ-002 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `verdict-card airgapped` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `guest-dispatch`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: REQ-003 vector-replay when feature is journey-steps

The app SHALL answer `vector-replay` when feature is journey-steps and no earlier rule matches, because journey steps are the acceptance vectors, replayed.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule3`).

#### Scenario: REQ-003 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `journey-steps online` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `vector-replay`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: REQ-004 model-record when feature is plain-reason

The app SHALL answer `model-record` when feature is plain-reason and no earlier rule matches, because the reason is read from the model the guest is built from.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule4`).

#### Scenario: REQ-004 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `plain-reason online`
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `model-record`, decided by REQ-004

### Requirement: REQ-005 model-record when feature is lexicon-panel

The app SHALL answer `model-record` when feature is lexicon-panel and no earlier rule matches, because the words are read from the product record.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule5`).

#### Scenario: REQ-005 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `lexicon-panel online` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `model-record`, decided by REQ-005

### Requirement: REQ-006 model-record when feature is rule-trace

The app SHALL answer `model-record` when feature is rule-trace and no earlier rule matches, because the rules and their citations are read from the model.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule6`).

#### Scenario: REQ-006 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `rule-trace airgapped` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `model-record`, decided by REQ-006

### Requirement: REQ-007 bundled-proof when feature is proof-panel and site is airgapped

The app SHALL answer `bundled-proof` when feature is proof-panel and site is airgapped and no earlier rule matches, because with no network the proof is read from the sources shipped with the site.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule7`).

#### Scenario: REQ-007 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `proof-panel airgapped` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `bundled-proof`, decided by REQ-007

### Requirement: REQ-008 attestation-link when feature is proof-panel

The app SHALL answer `attestation-link` when feature is proof-panel and no earlier rule matches, because online, the proof panel links the CI run that checked it.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule8`).

#### Scenario: REQ-008 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `proof-panel online` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `attestation-link`, decided by REQ-008

### Requirement: Otherwise model-record

The app SHALL answer `model-record` when no rule matches, because anything else is read from the static model record.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: No rule matches

- **WHEN** a request meets the conditions above
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `model-record`

### Requirement: The first matching rule decides

The app SHALL try REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-007, REQ-008 in that order, and the first rule that matches SHALL decide.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: Two rules match

- **WHEN** the request is `proof-panel airgapped` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `bundled-proof`, decided by REQ-007, the earlier rule

### Requirement: Request and answers

The app SHALL read one request as one line of 2 fields separated by single spaces, in this order, and SHALL answer exactly one of `guest-dispatch`, `model-record`, `vector-replay`, `fingerprint-check`, `bundled-proof`, `attestation-link`, or `invalid` for anything else.

| Field | Accepts | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `feature` | `verdict-card`, `plain-reason`, `rule-trace`, `proof-panel`, `journey-steps`, `lexicon-panel`, `seal-badge` | the front end feature to serve, as frontend-feature names it |
| `site` | `online`, `airgapped` | whether the site serving the page can reach the internet |

| Answer | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `guest-dispatch` | the verified WebAssembly guest computes the answer in the browser, through the router |
| `model-record` | the static model record the builder writes, site/app.json and the facet modules |
| `vector-replay` | the guest replays the acceptance vectors, so each journey step is a checked answer |
| `fingerprint-check` | the browser recomputes the holo fingerprint and compares it with the published one |
| `bundled-proof` | the LexLean proof sources shipped inside the site, readable with no network |
| `attestation-link` | a link to the CI run that checked the proofs, on GitHub |
| `invalid` | the request is malformed |

Verified: reading a request is tested, not proved.

#### Scenario: A malformed request is invalid

- **WHEN** the request is not 2 fields in this order
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `invalid`

## Out of scope

- Every capability runs in the reader's browser or is a static file of the site; there is no application server.
- Which feature a view shows is decided by frontend-feature.

## Examples

- `verdict-card airgapped` gives `guest-dispatch`
- `seal-badge online` gives `fingerprint-check`
- `proof-panel airgapped` gives `bundled-proof`
- `proof-panel online` gives `attestation-link`
- `journey-steps online` gives `vector-replay`
- `rule-trace airgapped` gives `model-record`
- `lexicon-panel online` gives `model-record`

## What is proved and what is tested

Lean proves each property marked proved above, for every request that decodes, with no exceptions and no sampling. The proof is about `judge`, the function the WebAssembly guest runs, because both come from the same model.

The parsing of requests is tested, not proved: the acceptance vectors in the app replay through the built guest, including malformed and oversized requests.

Nothing here says the rules are the right rules. That is the part only you can judge.

## Files

- `prism/spec.json` is this spec as data.
- `src/BackendCapability.lex.tex` is the LexLean model generated from it. It is the single source of the app.
